members.note: FDreamButtonStyle, resolved through StyleSource: the project sheet by default, this instance when told to.

The control takes UMG's FLinearColor and spends its ALPHA on its own RenderOpacity, which cascades to the face, the label and whatever else was put inside. Applied once at setup, never from the style pass: render opacity is a channel the host may also be driving, and a restyle that wrote 1 back over a fade would be a style pass undoing an animation. The colour half is deliberately not faked -- see UDreamBorder::ContentColorAndOpacity; BackgroundColor is the face's tint, which is the part a caller usually means.
FColor rather than FLinearColor, as every colour in this style family is. Multiplied over the face brush's own tint.
EDreamUIClickMethod; pushed onto the selectable underneath.
Every widget here carries it, so a control-level copy would shadow the base member and be a second answer to one question.

Only the mouse buttons in AcceptedMouseButtons press and click a button -- the left one alone by default, which is SButton's rule (its OnMouseButtonDown/Up test for EKeys::LeftMouseButton or a touch). UMG has no knob for it; AcceptedMouseButtons is this control's own, for a button that should answer another button too. A touch and a gamepad or keyboard press always count. A double click is two full clicks, as on SButton: the event system delivers the second press as a double click, and the button takes a double click as a press (SButton::OnMouseButtonDoubleClick hands it to OnMouseButtonDown).
Not for a mouse button the button does not answer (see OnClicked), nor while disabled.
Only after an OnPressed, as SButton's Release is gated on bIsPressed: the press pair always comes as a pair.
Same half-and-half as the property above.
Asked of the behaviour's selection state rather than remembered on the control.
Adds or destroys the face's UDreamUIDragSource, which is what gives a drag meaning here.
